🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin grinds against its heaviest supply wall near $80,000 as ETF inflows extend to an eighth straight session. Nvidia's blowout quarter lifted risk assets, while London and Washington moved on stablecoins and custody. 📈 Nvidia's blowout quarter spills into crypto Nvidia shares jumped roughly 8% after beating estimates and guiding to about $108 billion in revenue for next quarter, dragging technology stocks, AI infrastructure names and bitcoin higher with them. The move underlined how tightly crypto now trades alongside the AI-driven risk complex. Read full story 🏦 Bitcoin ETFs post eighth straight day of inflows US spot bitcoin funds have absorbed about $2.8 billion since the run began — the longest streak since April — while ether ETFs have matched them almost session for session. Three trading days remain for August to become the strongest month since October 2025. More details 🇬🇧 Britain hands the Bank of England a stablecoin mandate The UK government plans to give the Bank of England a new objective covering stablecoin innovation, with financial stability remaining its primary duty and annual reports to Parliament on the new remit. It is the clearest signal yet on how Britain intends to supervise payment tokens. Read more ⚖️ SEC revives the US crypto custody rule The regulator has pushed an overhaul of custody rules for investment advisers into White House review, resurrecting an effort the previous administration failed to land in 2023. The substance of the new approach remains largely undisclosed, leaving advisers guessing where client crypto may legally sit. See details 🚨 Emergency warning for Bitcoin Lightning node operators Core Lightning confirmed multiple vulnerabilities surfaced through AI-assisted bug reports, with developers holding technical details back for two weeks while fixes reach operators. It is the second Lightning security emergency this month traced to AI work on Bitcoin code. Read full story 🇰🇷 Mirae Asset targets a $109 billion crypto empire Founder Park Hyeon-joo laid out plans for Digital X, the exchange formerly known as Korbit, spanning stablecoins, tokenized real-world assets and security token offerings. The ambition drops one of South Korea's largest financial groups squarely into digital assets. More details 💠 Ripple Prime moves into US equity derivatives Ripple's prime brokerage arm
